title: Numerical conormal criterion at a prime of a finite type algebra
statement: Let k be a field and C a finite type commutative k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Fix a surjection pi:k[x_1,...,x_n] -> C, write I=ker(pi), and let q be a prime of C, with p=pi^{-1}(q). Then C_q is a complete-intersection local k-algebra [def-trf-complete-intersection-local] if and only if there is a natural number d with dim_q(Spec C)=d, d<=n, and dim_{kappa(p)}(kappa(p) tensor_{k[x]_p} (I/I^2)_p)=n-d [lem-trf-lci-conormal-fibre-field-change]. Dimensions here are local topological dimensions, not the Krull dimension of C_q.

proof.text: Replace the finite polynomial presentation by its quotient by the kernel. The quotient algebra equivalence identifies the contracted prime, its local ring and its local topological dimension. Localization and tensor cancellation identify the polynomial conormal fibre with the residue-field tensor product of the quotient conormal localization.

proof.text: A complete-intersection local presentation spreads to a principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood by lem-trf-ci-local-ring-principal-neighbourhood. The conormal rank theorem supplies a basis of size n-d and d<=n. Base change of this basis to the residue field proves the numerical equality.

proof.text: Conversely, the conormal localization is finite over the Noetherian polynomial quotient local ring. Lift a residue-field basis of n-d elements to module elements and apply Nakayama to obtain local generators. The conormal-generator criterion gives a principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood. Its dimension integer equals d by equality of the local topological dimensions.

source.place: Tags 00SC (lemma-lci), 00SF (lemma-lci-local), 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime); numerical conormal criterion used in Tag 00SI.

proof.text: Choose a polynomial quotient presentation of that neighbourhood. Pull its prime back through the presentation. The equations are regular in the polynomial local ring by the global-complete-intersection regular-sequence theorem, and lie in its maximal ideal. Localization of the quotient and iterated localization identify their quotient with the desired local ring. Lift the regular local ring to the universe required by IsCompleteIntersectionLocal and transport the list and quotient equivalence. This proves the reverse implication, including empty lists.

theorem isCompleteIntersectionLocal_iff_conormal_finrank
    (k : Type u) (C : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing C] [Algebra k C]
    [FiniteType k C] (n : ℕ) (π : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] C)
    (hπ : Function.Surjective π) (q : Ideal C) [q.IsPrime] :
    IsCompleteIntersectionLocal k (Localization.AtPrime q) ↔
      ∃ d : ℕ,
        topologicalKrullDimAt (⟨q, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum C) =
          (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ d ≤ n ∧
        Module.finrank (q.comap π.toRingHom).ResidueField
          (AlgebraicGeometry.lciConormalFibre (q.comap π.toRingHom)
            (RingHom.ker π.toRingHom)) = n - d
